newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Mediterranean investment fund reports fast growth.
newsitem.headline: Mediterranean investment fund reports fast growth.

text.p: Mediterranean Emergence SICAV, a new emerging markets open-ended investment fund, said on Tuesday it registered a return of more than 45 percent over the last six months.
The fund has $12 million of capital, subscribed mainly by European institutional investors and invested in the stock exchanges of Tunisia, Morocco, Egypt, Jordan and Lebanon.

It was launched last August by Tunis-based International Maghreb Merchant Bank (IMBank), and France's Societe Marseillaise de Credit (SMC) and Societe Generale de Placement-Banque (GP Bank). It is managed under the French law by SMC and advised by IMBank.

"Mediterranee Emergence was ranked first international SICAV by Paris-based rating agencies Micropal and Europerformance with a return of above 45 percent over a period of six months," fund manager Lilia Abdelwahed told Reuters.

"These positive performances and the good behaviour of some emerging markets in the area demonstrate that the south-Mediterranean region is potentially a zone of productive and profitable investment," Abdelwahed said.

IMBank is the first merchant bank to have been set up so far in North Africa, in the belief that emerging markets in the region and elsewhere in the Middle East offer large potential for trade and project finance. It was founded in 1995 with a capital of $3 million.

Shareholders include prominent Maghrebi and European businessmen and financiers including IMBank's chairman Moncef Cheikhrouhou and general manager Adel Dajani, together with GP Bank, SMC, and the World Bank's International Finance Corporation (IFC).
Shareholders also include Creditanstalt Finanziaria Spa., the Italian merchant banking subsidiary of Credistantalt Bankverein of Austria.
